subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum — resale & training-use language
messages:
From: Elena Torres <e.torres@acmesolutions.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmesolutions.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CCPA addendum — question on resale / training usage

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and privacy teams asked us to confirm two items before we can advance to a PO:

1) Resale / redistribution: the vendor questionnaire flags a clause about whether the vendor "may resell or otherwise disclose Personal Information to third parties." We need a clear contractual commitment that Redwood will not resell Acme customer data or include it in secondary productized datasets.

2) Model training / improvement: can you confirm whether Redwood uses customer text data to further train or improve models that are served to other customers? If so, we need opt-out language or an express prohibition for regulated data categories under California law.

Attached is our template US privacy addendum (Acme_US_Privacy_Addendum_v1.docx). Can you provide a short response and confirm what evidence you can share (e.g., subprocessors list, SOC 2, data flow diagram, telemetry retention)?

We have a soft target for procurement sign-off by 2027-04-08.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Privacy & Policy
Acme Solutions
[Attachment: Acme_US_Privacy_Addendum_v1.docx (DOCX)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <e.torres@acmesolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA addendum — question on resale / training usage

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the template. Short answers up front:

1) Resale: Redwood does not resell customer data. We act as a service provider / processor; contractual language can reflect that and prohibit any resale or sale-based commercialization of Acme customer data.

2) Model training: By default our hosted offering uses telemetry and aggregated signals to improve operational performance (e.g., latency, tokenization heuristics), but we do not use customer payloads to train or update base models that are redistributed. For customers requiring a strict prohibition, we support a contractual opt-out: no training or derivative model usage of any data classified as Personal Information.

Evidence we can share immediately:
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted)
- current subprocessor roster (CSV) — we manage subprocessors in-region where required
- high-level data flow diagram and telemetry retention policy

I'll loop in Marissa and Karthik to propose precise DPA language and provide the redlines back to you. Attached is an initial internal note (redwood-dpa-notes-20270402.pdf) that maps our standard positions to common enterprise asks.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dpa-notes-20270402.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <e.torres@acmesolutions.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA addendum — proposed redlines (attached)

Elena —

Thanks — I've reviewed Acme's addendum and drafted redlines that: 1) explicitly classify Redwood as a "Service Provider/Processor" (not a Business), 2) add a carve-out preventing Redwood from using Personal Information to create productized datasets or to sell/redistribute data, and 3) add explicit language opting Acme out of any training/derivative-model use for Personal Information.

Key edits called out in the attachment (redwood-dpa-redlines-20270402.pdf):
- Section 2(b): service provider definition + operational restrictions
- Section 4(c): explicit prohibition on resale or transfer for marketing/commercialization
- New Section 7: "Model Training; Derivative Works" — "Redwood will not use Personal Information to train models or produce derivative datasets made available to third parties where such use is prohibited by Customer. Customer may require an explicit opt-out via writing."
- Subprocessor flow: 30-day notice before onboarding, emergency onboarding process documented

Please see the attached PDF for the redline. If that looks good I can produce a Word redline and a clean DPA for countersignature.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dpa-redlines-20270402.pdf (PDF)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <e.torres@acmesolutions.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA addendum — telemetry & subprocessor cadence

Hi Elena — quick operational notes to supplement Marissa's legal edits: 

- Telemetry / logs: operational telemetry (timestamps, request latencies, error rates) retained 90 days by default; request/response payloads retained per customer-configured retention settings. We can offer a 30-day maximum retention for payloads on the hosted plan for customers who require tighter retention.
- Subprocessors: current roster attached (scoped-subprocessors-20270403.csv). We provide 30-day notice for routine onboarding and immediate notice + mitigation plan for emergency subprocessors.
- Data exports / backup: backups are encrypted at rest and we can provide audit logs showing exports tied to customer tenant IDs (useful for procurement).

If Acme needs stricter telemetry retention (for example, no payload persistence), we can propose a deployment configuration or an enterprise-only Dedicated/Private plan where telemetry/payloads are not persisted beyond session windows. Happy to discuss specifics.

Karthik
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: scoped-subprocessors-20270403.csv (CSV)]

From: Elena Torres <e.torres@acmesolutions.com>

Date: Mon, 04 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA addendum — resale & training-use language

Team —

Thank you for the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple of final items before legal will sign: 

- Please convert the PDF redlines into a Word redline and a clean DPA for countersignature (we need track changes).
- We will propose language for the opt-out field: a one-sentence checkbox in the SOW that prohibits use of Personal Information for training or derivative productization. Can Redwood accept that as a binding contractual instruction?
- Procurement also requested a DocuSign link for countersignature and a standard PO format. I'll route the PO after countersign.

If you can get the Word redline and DocuSign by EOD 2027-04-05, we should be able to finish procurement next week.

Best,
Elena
Head of Privacy & Policy
Acme Solutions
